nodes.label: Concept
nodes.text: Concept The database (SQL) is the core every data career passes through (Excel → SQL → Python → Data Analyst / Data Engineer / Data Scientist). Following Grok's principle — the black hole is never drawn, only the light around it — the database is not drawn as a shape; it is the void at the centre of a disc of light. The void is the "unknown" that data science and AI explore; the three traced layers make it read instantly as a database.

nodes.label: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`)
nodes.text: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`) ```svg <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"> <circle class="disc" cx="50" cy="50" r="46" fill="#f4f4f4"/> <path class="void" d="M29 31C29 17 71 17 71 31V69C71 83 29 83 29 69Z" fill="#000"/> <g class="bands" fill="none" stroke="#f4f4f4" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"> <path d="M29 31C29 45 71 45 71 31"/> <!-- top rim --> <path d="M29 45C29 59 71 59 71 45"/> <!-- layer 1 --> <path d="M29 59C29 73 71 73 71 59"/> <!-- layer 2 --> </g> </svg> ``` Keep the class names (`disc`, `void`, `bands`) — the animation depends on them.

nodes.label: Usage rules
nodes.text: Usage rules - Default: white logo on black. Use `logo-light-bg.svg` only on light surfaces. - The void must always be the background colour (it is a hole, not a black shape). On a non-black background, use the inline version and set `--logo-bg` to that background. - Minimum size 16 px. Clear space around it = ¼ of its width. - No outlines, glows, gradients, rotation or added elements (stars, sparkles were tried and removed on purpose). - Wordmark: datafromzero, lowercase, Geist 500, letter-spacing −0.01em, to the right of the mark; tagline *From A1 to AI* in Geist Mono when space allows. ---

nodes.label: Build notes for Astro Starlight
nodes.text: Build notes for Astro Starlight Priorities (in order): stability & speed → mobile-first (most readers are on phones) → nice motion. - Where GSAP is allowed: homepage and story / history / visualization pages only. Not on lessons, exercises or reference pages — those stay plain Starlight for speed. - Homepage: build it as a custom Astro page (its own layout, not the docs layout), port the prototype into components, and load GSAP only there (`<script>` inside the page/component so it is bundled per-page). - GSAP: `npm i gsap` (3.13+; all plugins are free now). Allowed: `ScrollTrigger`, `SplitText`, `DrawSVG` (SPEC D22). Use `gsap.matchMedia()` for reduced-motion and pointer checks, and kill ScrollTriggers on page leave if client-side navigation is enabled. - Starlight config: use `logo/logo-dark-bg.svg` as the site logo (with a light-theme variant `logo-light-bg.svg` if light mode is kept) and `logo/favicon.svg` as the favicon. Site name = placeholder. - Docs area look: apply the tokens in §2 (black background, Geist / Geist Mono) through Starlight's custom CSS so lessons and reference match the homepage. Two modes: - Study / lessons: open, quiet, one idea per screen, generous spacing. - Reference: book-like, indexed, searchable (Starlight's built-in search), compact. - Math: DS / Statistics pages need LaTeX — add `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` (and KaTeX CSS). - Fonts: self-host or use Google Fonts with `display=swap`; preload Geist 400. - Performance budget: homepage JS (GSAP + plugins + page code) ≈ 90 KB gzipped max (SPEC D22); no images required — everything is SVG/CSS. Content must be fully readable with JS disabled (GSAP sets hidden states, CSS never hides content by default — the prototype already works this way). ---

Never on lessons, reference, datasets or project pages. - Every animation respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; all content is visible with JS disabled. - Page-to-page navigation uses CSS-only cross-document View Transitions (D26) and Speculation Rules prefetch (D27); neither adds executable JS to lesson pages. - Study pages (lessons): wide line-height, max ~70ch, one idea per section. Reference pages: compact, scannable, fixed section order (§5.2). ---

nodes.label: Analytics & privacy
nodes.text: Analytics & privacy - Google Analytics 4, loaded only after consent (Consent Mode v2, default `denied`). - A minimal consent banner (Accept / Decline), choice remembered; "Cookie settings" link in the footer to change it. - Declining must leave the site fully functional; GA script must never block rendering. - The Measurement ID is the single value `GA_ID` in `src/site.ts`. While it is empty there is no banner, no GA code, no "Cookie settings" link and no added JavaScript. The choice is kept in `localStorage` key `dfz-consent`; only page views are collected for now. - `/privacy/` page states what is collected, why, retention, and how to opt out. - Events worth tracking (optional): `open_in_colab`, `open_in_sheets`, `show_solution`, `report_issue`. > Note: GA plus a banner costs some speed and simplicity; it was chosen for richer insight. > If the banner hurts the experience, GoatCounter (no cookies, no banner) is the drop-in fallback. ---

nodes.label: Content production (replaces migration, D24)
nodes.text: Content production (replaces migration, D24) Content is written from scratch; `johnha912/data-odyssey` is not migrated. 1. Curriculum map. Research proposes every lesson per stage (id, slug, title, order, level, duration, objectives, prerequisites, key sources). The owner approves the map once; slugs then become permanent (§3). 2. Stubs. Approved lessons are created as `status: draft` files (never deployed, D18). The build validates ids, prerequisites and cycles from day one. 3. Writing. The owner writes the lesson text. The team adds or completes frontmatter, exercises and solutions, notebooks, Google Sheets templates, datasets (§7), `Term` links and sources, and keeps the build green. 4. Publishing. The owner reviews and sets `status: published`. Vietnamese translations follow in later PRs (§8). 5. Release. Tag `v1.0.0` once the four core stages are published; enable Zenodo; publish `CITATION.cff` (§9).

nodes.label: Slug rules
nodes.text: Slug rules - Lowercase English, kebab-case, ASCII only: `/sql/window-functions/`. Vietnamese pages reuse the English slug. - No numbers, dates or versions in slugs. Order comes from `order` in frontmatter. - Always a trailing slash (`trailingSlash: 'always'`). - The slug is derived from the file name; the file name is the slug.

nodes.label: Change rules
nodes.text: Change rules - Never rename or delete a published URL. If a rename is unavoidable: 1. add an entry to `src/redirects.ts` (old → new), 2. keep the lesson `id` unchanged (§5.1), 3. note it in `CHANGELOG.md`. - A retired page stays online with `status: deprecated` and a link to its replacement. - Anchors (`#heading-id`) on reference pages are part of the contract — headings there are not renamed casually.

nodes.label: Linking inside content
nodes.text: Linking inside content - Internal links are root-relative (`/sql/joins/`), never absolute (`https://datafromzero.github.io/…`). - Link to other lessons by path; the build validates every internal link (§12). ---

nodes.label: Information architecture
nodes.text: Information architecture ``` datafromzero ├─ Learn (Study mode — open, quiet, one idea per screen) │ ├─ 1 Excel / Sheets → 2 SQL → 3 Python → 4 Advanced core │ └─ Branches: Data Analyst · Data Engineer · Data Scientist · Analytics Engineer · ML/AI Engineer ├─ Reference (Book mode — indexed, compact, searchable) │ ├─ Glossary │ ├─ Syntax: Excel functions · SQL keywords · pandas │ ├─ Statistics formulas │ └─ Careers (5 guides) ├─ Stories (history, explainers, visualizations — motion allowed) ├─ Datasets └─ About · Cite · Changelog · License · Privacy ``` Sidebar order and grouping are generated from frontmatter (`stage`, `order`), never hand-maintained. ---

nodes.label: Content model
nodes.text: Content model Schemas are registered in `src/content.config.ts` and defined in `src/lib/content-schemas.ts`; validation runs on every build (`src/lib/content-validation.ts`). Adding an optional field = MINOR change. Adding a required field, renaming or removing a field = MAJOR change + migration script. Rules for every type (D17): - `id` is lowercase kebab-case (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`) and unique across all content types (an English page and its Vietnamese translation share one id). - The file's folder decides its type (paths in the headings below). A file nested deeper than its type allows fails the build. - Every id reference must point to an existing entry of the right type. - `sources[].url` and `sheet` must be `http(s)` URLs. - The build reports all problems at once, naming the file and field, and fails.

nodes.label: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: sql-joins # permanent internal key; never changes, even if the slug does title: Joining tables description: Combine rows from two tables with INNER and LEFT JOIN. # ≤ 160 chars, used for SEO/social stage: sql # excel | sql | python | core | data-analyst | data-engineer | # data-scientist | analytics-engineer | ml-engineer order: 40 # sort key inside the stage; use gaps of 10 so lessons can be inserted level: beginner # beginner | intermediate | advanced duration: 25 # minutes, integer objectives: # 2–5 items, each starts with a verb - Explain what a join key is - Write an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN prerequisites: # lesson ids (not URLs); validated at build time - sql-select-basics datasets: [cafe-sales] # dataset names (§7); optional notebook: notebooks/sql/sql-joins.ipynb # optional; drives the "Open in Colab" button sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/…/copy # optional; Excel stage "Make a copy" link reviewed: 2026-11-15 # last date the content was checked for correctness sources: # at least 1; documentation, papers, books - title: PostgreSQL documentation — Joined tables url: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-table-expressions.html status: published # draft | published | deprecated replaced_by: null # lesson id, required when status = deprecated --- ``` - `stage` must match the lesson's folder. - `status: draft` lessons are built only in local dev, never deployed (D18). A published or deprecated lesson may not list a draft in `prerequisites` or `replaced_by`. - A deprecated lesson shows a notice linking to `replaced_by` (§3.3). Rendered at the top of every lesson: level · duration · last reviewed, then Objectives and Before this lesson (prerequisite links). Rendered at the bottom: Unlocks next (the lessons that list this one in `prerequisites`, drafts excluded, in the reader's language, computed at build time without JavaScript; hidden when empty), Sources, Cite this lesson, Suggest an edit, Report an issue, prev/next. - Inside one stage, `order` must be a topological order of `prerequisites`: a prerequisite in the same stage has a smaller `order`. Prerequisite cycles fail the check (`scripts/check-graph.ts`, §12).

nodes.label: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: ref-sql-group-by title: GROUP BY area: sql # excel | sql | pandas | stats summary: Groups rows that share values so aggregates are computed per group. syntax: | # optional, shown in a code block at the top SELECT col, AGG(x) FROM t GROUP BY col; see_also: [ref-sql-having, glossary-aggregate] # ids used_in: [sql-aggregation] # lesson ids; optional (can also be computed) reviewed: 2026-11-15 sources: [ … ] --- ``` Reference pages use a fixed section order: Syntax → Parameters → Examples → Common mistakes → See also. `area` must match the folder. `see_also` is required (an empty list is allowed); its ids may be reference entries or glossary terms. `used_in` must name existing lessons that are not drafts (D18).

nodes.label: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: glossary-primary-key term: Primary key short: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row. # ≤ 140 chars, used in hover/inline tooltips aliases: [PK] # required; an empty list is allowed reviewed: 2026-11-15 --- ``` `term` is also used as the page title.

nodes.label: Career guide, Story, Dataset
nodes.text: Career guide, Story, Dataset - Career (`/careers/{career}/`): `id`, `title`, `summary`, `skills[]`, `stages[]` (which stages/branches to finish), `reviewed`, `sources[]`. - Story (`/stories/{slug}/`): `id`, `title`, `description`, `published`, `reviewed`, `sources[]`, `motion: true|false`. - Dataset (`/datasets/{name}/`): files are defined in §7. Page frontmatter is not defined yet (D19); until it is, the build rejects dataset pages other than `datasets/index`. ---

nodes.label: Authoring components
nodes.text: Authoring components The only components content may use. Each must degrade to readable static HTML without JS. | Component | Purpose | No-JS fallback | |---|---|---| | `<Exercise id="sql-joins-1">` … `</Exercise>` | Numbered exercise block | Plain block | | `<Solution>` … `</Solution>` (inside `Exercise`) | Hidden answer, "Show solution" | Native `<details>` | | `<OpenInColab />` | Button from the lesson's `notebook` field | Plain link | | `<OpenInSheets />` | "Make a copy" button from the lesson's `sheet` field | Plain link | | `<Term id="glossary-primary-key">primary key</Term>` | Inline glossary link with short definition | Plain link | | Starlight `<Aside>` (note / tip / caution / danger) | Callouts | Built in | | `$…$`, `$$…$$` | Math (KaTeX) | MathML | Rules: - No other components or raw `<script>` in content. New components are added here first (MINOR change). - Components are available in every `.mdx` file without import lines (D21). The build fails, naming the file and line, on any `import`/`export` in content, any component not in this table, any `<script>`, event-handler attribute (`on…=`), `set:html` or `javascript:` URL (in `.md` or `.mdx`), a `Solution` outside an `Exercise`, or math inside a heading. - `Term` shows the definition as a native popover, with no JS: opened by hover/focus where interest invokers exist (`interestfor`), otherwise by a small "?" button next to the link (`popovertarget`, tap or click). Both dismiss with Esc or an outside click; the link always goes to the glossary page. - A literal dollar sign in prose must be written `\$`; otherwise `$…$` is read as math. - Exercise ids are permanent (`{lesson-id}-{n}`) so teachers can reference "Exercise sql-joins-2".

nodes.label: Future in-browser code (not now)
nodes.text: Future in-browser code (not now) Write runnable examples as fenced code blocks with a meta flag: ```` ```sql dataset=cafe-sales ````. They render as normal code today; a future `RunnableCode` enhancement (DuckDB-WASM / Pyodide) can pick them up without editing content. ---

nodes.label: Datasets
nodes.text: Datasets ``` datasets/ cafe-sales/ v1/ orders.csv customers.csv README.md # description, columns, types, row counts, how it was generated, license schema.yaml # machine-readable column definitions ``` - A small set of synthetic datasets the author creates, reused from Excel through Python so learners see the same data in every tool. No personal data. - Immutable once released. A change in columns or values = new folder `v2/`; `v1/` stays forever, so old notebooks and spreadsheets keep working. - Notebooks load data from a release-tag URL, not `main`: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/v1.0.0/datasets/cafe-sales/v1/orders.csv` - Each dataset also ships an `.xlsx` (Excel stage) and a `.sql` load script (SQL stage) generated by a script in `scripts/`. - License: CC BY 4.0. Notebooks: `notebooks/{stage}/{lesson-id}.ipynb`, opened via `https://colab.research.google.com/github/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/blob/main/notebooks/…`. Notebooks are cleared of outputs before commit (CI check). ---

nodes.label: Internationalization
nodes.text: Internationalization - Starlight i18n with `root` locale English and `vi` locale. UI strings translated in `src/content/i18n/vi.json`. - Vietnamese files mirror English paths: `src/content/docs/vi/sql/joins.md` with the same `id`. - Untranslated pages fall back to English with Starlight's "not yet translated" notice. - A translation records `translated_from_version` (curriculum version it was translated from) so stale translations can be listed. It is required on every Vietnamese page of a typed collection (§5), and the page must have an English counterpart at the mirrored path with the same `id`. - Code, SQL keywords and dataset column names stay in English in both languages. ---

nodes.label: Versioning, citation, changelog
nodes.text: Versioning, citation, changelog - Curriculum version (SemVer), tagged on GitHub as `vX.Y.Z`: - MAJOR — curriculum restructure, a required schema change, or any URL redirect batch - MINOR — new lessons, reference entries, datasets, components, optional fields - PATCH — corrections, clarifications, link fixes - Each GitHub Release is archived by Zenodo (GitHub integration) → one concept DOI (always latest) + one DOI per version. - `CITATION.cff` at repo root (title, author, version, date, concept DOI, license). Updated on every release. - `/cite/` page: APA + BibTeX for the whole work, generated at build time from `CITATION.cff` (the build fails if its `version` differs from `package.json`); the DOI line reads "after the first release" until Zenodo exists, then shows the concept DOI and per-version DOIs. - Every lesson footer shows Cite this lesson: author, year (from `reviewed`), title, site, curriculum version, URL. Static pages cannot know when they were read, so a note asks the reader to add their access date (D20). - `CHANGELOG.md` follows *Keep a Changelog*; `/changelog/` renders it (single source, no copy); `/license/` shows `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-CONTENT` the same way. - The site footer shows the current version and its DOI badge. ---

Wraps Starlight's docs loader: After loading, EVERY entry is validated against the schema for its content type and the cross-file rules are checked (unique ids, prerequisites, replacements, translations). Per-file rules for every entry (schema, folder match, location, Vietnamese version). English pages own the ids. Ids are unique across all content types. Id references, drafts and replacements are shared with scripts/check-graph.ts (graph.ts).

nodes.label: home-boot.ts
nodes.text: First-load homepage script (about 1 KB). It never imports GSAP statically: the hero entrance is CSS, and the scroll choreography is fetched after the page has loaded (or on first interaction). Drop the reveal mask once the ripple has finished, so the grid is a plain layer again. Tap or click the hero logo to replay its intro. Restarting CSS animations needs one style flush. Motion is an enhancement: the page is already complete without it.

nodes.label: gsap.ts
nodes.text: Single entry to GSAP for the homepage. Imported only from the deferred motion chunks, so the library never sits on the critical path. Plugins are registered by the modules that use them. The mobile address bar resizing the viewport must not trigger a refresh while scrolling.

nodes.label: motion.ts
nodes.text: Deferred homepage motion: nav, scroll progress, hero scroll-out, pointer effects, and the lazy per-section timelines. Everything is inside gsap.matchMedia(), so reduced motion gets none of it (and in practice never even loads this chunk). Create a section's timelines only when it is within one viewport of the screen (one shared, code-split module). Scroll progress hairline: native scroll-driven CSS animation where supported, ScrollTrigger otherwise. Hero drifts away as the page scrolls (design/README.md §5): one scrubbed timeline. Nav: hides while reading down, returns on any upward scroll or keyboard focus. Section timelines, created on demand and code-split. Fonts change text metrics once: re-measure a single time. Pointer effects: fine pointers only (mouse and trackpad), never touch. The glow center eases toward the pointer; only style writes happen per frame. Measure once (document coordinates), refresh with ScrollTrigger; pointermove only reads event data. Magnetic buttons.

nodes.label: native.ts
nodes.text: True where CSS scroll-driven animations run the progress bar and rail fill (see home.css). Elsewhere the GSAP ScrollTrigger scrubs take over.

nodes.label: marquee.ts
nodes.text: Marquee: loops forever, runs only while visible, speeds up and leans with scroll velocity. Resuming with the button focused must actually resume: ignore focus until it leaves. Only keyboard focus holds the loop (a mouse click on the toggle must not).
